newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia cenbank sees budget deficit a step back.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia cenbank sees budget deficit a step back.

text.p: Bank of Slovenia governor France Arhar said the budget deficit forecast for this year was a backward step for Slovenia's economy and its ambitions to join the European Union as soon as possible.

"The expected budget deficit is a step back because a balanced budget is the best for further stabilisation (of the economy) and for the way to Europe," Arhar told Slovenian daily newspaper Delo in an interview published on Thursday.
The government on Monday adopted a budget proposal according to which 1997 spending would be 737.9 billion tolars ($4.4 billion), resulting in a deficit of 27.9 billion.
In 1996 budget spending was 597.5 billion tolars, with a surplus of 16.3 billion tolars.

"In the past five years when the budget was harmonised it had a stabilising effect. A small economy with a budget deficit will represent a minus abroad and a reason for lower confidence (in Slovenia)," Arhar said.
Arhar also said Slovenia should start restructuring its pension system which currently relies almost solely on the public pension scheme and exerts large pressure on the budget.
"It is necessary to start a debate on reforming the pension system in order to reduce general costs," Arhar said. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 168.5 Slovenian Tolars)
